refutation_attempt: Searched every TARGET test and the C ABI for pattern calls: StorageSmoke.c passes lev*, z*, *.dat and *.png through the same GlobMatch, so 'nothing tests the overloads' and 'passes a zero-length pattern' are false. Byte-wise ? and case-sensitivity re-derived from the matcher and XNA IL.
reason: The matcher defect stands: ? consumes one UTF-8 byte and the compare is case-sensitive, against XNA's single-character wildcard and file-system case rules. But star patterns over ASCII names are tested via the C ABI smoke test, so only ?, non-ASCII and case are untested.

correction.title: StorageContainer::GetFileNames/GetDirectoryNames(searchPattern): GlobMatch treats ? as one byte and compares case-sensitively on every host
correction.summary: The hand-written matcher behind the pattern overloads matches ? against one UTF-8 byte rather than one character and compares bytes case-sensitively even on Windows, where XNA's Directory.GetFiles matching is not; only star patterns over ASCII names are exercised by any test, and only through the C ABI smoke test.
correction.actual: GlobMatch is a 22-line backtracking matcher in an anonymous namespace of modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp; its own comment says '?' = any single char. It compares bytes of the UTF-8 file name: ? consumes exactly one byte, so a non-ASCII character (two to four bytes) needs as many ?; every other byte, the dot included, matches only itself, case-sensitively on every host. "?.sav" therefore misses é.sav, and "slot?.sav" misses SLOT1.SAV on Windows, where the file system treats the two spellings as one name and XNA would return it. No C++ storage test calls either pattern overload. The only test that does is the C ABI smoke test (modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/StorageSmoke.c, registered as CApi_StorageSmoke only when CNA_BUILD_C_API is ON; it is OFF by default and no workflow at TARGET enables it), which checks the star patterns lev*, z*, *.dat and *.png against ASCII names. The ? wildcard, non-ASCII names and case are not tested anywhere.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp, the tests and the C adapter at 009d40f5; not executed. The byte and case behaviour follows mechanically from the matcher's single comparison (pattern[pi] == '?' || pattern[pi] == str[si]). The XNA side is from xna4-spec's StorageContainer documentation and the decompiled StorageContainer (Directory.GetFiles/GetDirectories). The earlier text said that nothing tests the overloads and that the C smoke test passes only a zero-length pattern; that is wrong: StorageSmoke.c's directory and file cases pass non-empty star patterns, and CNA's own tools/c-api/coverage_mappings.json records 'glob and empty-pattern listings'. StorageDeviceTests.cpp (14 tests) still never calls the pattern overloads. .NET Framework's pattern matching has further legacy rules (short-name and three-letter-extension matches, and *.* matching names without a dot) that CNA does not reproduce; they were not examined and are not part of this entry.

refutation_attempt: Looked for compensation: grepped all callers of SetAppNameEXT/GetStorageRootEXT/EnsureStorageRoot; nothing in Game or the runtime resolves the root at startup, and no lock or atomic exists. Checked the header for a single-thread contract (none). Checked CNA-BUG-151 overlap: it is the single-threaded latch, not the race.
reason: Statement order and three plain statics re-derived: a second thread sees the flag set and returns the still-empty root by reference. Real, reachable when SetAppNameEXT is never called. The failed-resolution sentence and unwritable-root test variant are CNA-BUG-151's defect, which stays separate; not a duplicate.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the three sites use the narrow path constructor while siblings use PathFromUtf8. Searched for a UTF-8 code-page manifest that would neutralise it (none). Found the trigger understated (any non-ASCII byte misreads) and a C ABI test that calls the properties.
reason: Real and matches path-model rule 2, but the Windows effect is inferred from the standard library's narrow conversion, not run. The trigger is any non-ASCII character (a CP1252-representable e-acute is two bytes and misreads too). CApi_StorageSmoke exercises the three properties on an ASCII root only.

correction.actual: In modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp, getFreeSpaceProperty and getTotalSpaceProperty call fs::exists(root) and fs::space(root) with the std::string root, and getIsConnectedProperty builds fs::path p(root). On POSIX the bytes pass through unchanged. On Windows the narrow constructor reads the string through the process ANSI code page, so every non-ASCII character in the root, including one the code page can spell (the two UTF-8 bytes of e-acute become two other characters), yields a different path. That affects a root containing such a character in the user profile path, in LOCALAPPDATA or in the application name given to SetAppNameEXT: fs::exists reports false, the space properties return LLONG_MAX ("unlimited") instead of the real figure, and getIsConnectedProperty walks up from the wrong path.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp and the path model at 009d40f5; not exercised on Windows. Every other path in modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp and modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp converts with PathFromUtf8, and EnsureStorageRoot reads the environment with GetEnvironmentVariableW precisely so that non-ASCII roots survive; these three properties are the remaining narrow sites in the module. The Windows consequence rests on the standard library's narrow-to-wide conversion through the ANSI code page: CNA's own spikes/windows-unicode-path-spike records the ANSI behaviour of path::string() and of fopen given UTF-8 bytes (which fails for representable names such as cafe with an accent too) but did not measure the path(std::string) constructor itself, and a search of the tree finds no manifest that sets a UTF-8 active code page. The basis is therefore inferred, not executed. Tests: CApi_StorageSmoke (C ABI builds only) calls the free-space, total-space and connection queries on an ASCII root; nothing runs them on a non-ASCII root.

refutation_attempt: Traced DeleteContainer('GamerServices') through ResolveContainedPath: a non-root child passes, so no guard stops it. Read LocalGamerServicesStore StoreRoot (root/GamerServices) and that achievements are read from disk on each query. Searched published entries for the same collision (none).
reason: Both the store and a container titled GamerServices resolve to <root>/GamerServices, and DeleteContainer remove_alls it. Nothing reserves the name and the header documents the subdirectory. Tests cover DeleteContainer and the store separately, with different app names, never the collision.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a type check before fs::remove in both methods and in the C adapter (none). Read the decompiled XNA: DeleteFile is File.Delete and DeleteDirectory is Directory.Delete after ValidateArguments, so the type refusals and missing-directory throw are real. Checked whether tests pin the deletes.
reason: Both methods call fs::remove(ResolveNativePath(...)), which removes a file or an empty directory and returns false for a missing entry, so DeleteFile removes a directory and DeleteDirectory a file. Tests exist only for the escaping-path refusal and the C ABI happy path; none checks entry type.

refutation_attempt: Checked every member and the C adapter for a disposed guard (none); read decompiled XNA (VerifyNotDisposed in ValidateArguments, getters, listings). Looked for tests: the C ABI smoke test disposes containers and pins that file_exists still works inside the Disposing callback.
reason: XNA divergence is real: no member checks isDisposed_. But the entry's 'Tests: None' is wrong, and a CNA test (CABI-34 in StorageSmoke.c) pins member use inside the Disposing callback, so the suggested fix would break it unless that ordering is kept or changed deliberately.

correction.actual: StorageContainer::Dispose in modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp sets isDisposed_ and raises Disposing once; nothing else reads the flag except getIsDisposedProperty and the destructor. CreateFile, OpenFile, DeleteFile, CreateDirectory, DeleteDirectory, FileExists, DirectoryExists, both name listings and both getters behave exactly as before disposal. FNA's container has no disposal check either, so CNA follows FNA rather than XNA here. Streams opened before Dispose stay valid, which matches XNA (they are independent streams) and is not part of this defect; the FileShare point the candidate also raised is published as CNA-GAP-048. One CNA test pins part of the current behaviour: the C ABI smoke test (CABI-34, modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/StorageSmoke.c) requires a container to answer file_exists from inside its own Disposing callback, which runs after the flag is set, so any fix has to keep that callback window usable or change that test deliberately; XNA itself would throw there.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp and its header at 009d40f5; not executed. XNA's behaviour is from the decompiled StorageContainer (VerifyNotDisposed); FNA's from a local reference checkout of FNA's src/Storage/StorageContainer.cs. The C ABI inherits the behaviour: cna_storage_container_dispose disposes "without releasing its handle", GetContainer does not consult the flag, and the other container routes forward to the same members. Tests: no test calls a member after Dispose() has returned, and StorageDeviceTests.cpp never disposes a container explicitly. CApi_StorageSmoke (C ABI builds only) does exercise Dispose, IsDisposed and the exactly-once Disposing event, and its CABI-34 ordering case asserts that FileExists succeeds from inside the Disposing callback. Independently observed as a separate finding (merged): Dispose only sets isDisposed_; no member consults it, so file and directory operations still run on a disposed container.

refutation_attempt: Grepped all non-doc TARGET code for DeviceChanged: only the definition and the C adapter's Add/Remove. Read decompiled XNA (OnDeviceChanged wired to FrameworkCallbackLinker; raised from FrameworkDispatcher.Update on a native System_DeviceChanged call). Found a C ABI test that subscribes and unsubscribes.
reason: The gap stands: nothing raises the event; XNA's raise comes from native device-change callbacks with no desktop counterpart here. But 'Tests: None' is wrong: CApi_StorageSmoke subscribes, unsubscribes and checks stale-registration refusal, though nothing can make the event fire.

correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 and the decompiled XNA 4.0 Storage IL and FrameworkDispatcher; not executed. In XNA the static constructor wires StorageDevice.OnDeviceChanged to FrameworkCallbackLinker.StorageDeviceChanged, which FrameworkDispatcher.Update raises when a native System_DeviceChanged call was queued; the documented meaning is 'a device is removed or inserted'. No managed source of that call exists in the decompiled assemblies, so how often genuine XNA raises it on Windows is not established. Tests: CApi_StorageSmoke (C ABI builds only) subscribes, unsubscribes and checks stale-registration refusal for the event, but no test can make it fire because nothing in CNA raises it.

refutation_attempt: Read OpenFile: the share parameter is unnamed and FileStream gets only path, mode, access. Searched TARGET and the sibling Sharp Runtime history for a FileShare-taking FileStream (none). Checked the C route and CNA's own docs, which say the container ignores the share selection.
reason: The share mode is discarded and Sharp Runtime's FileStream has no share parameter, so None, Read and ReadWrite behave alike. CNA's own docs/c-api/STORAGE.md and FEATURE_MATRIX.md record the limitation, which supports the gap class. The Sharp Runtime signature comes from an unpinned sibling checkout.

refutation_attempt: Searched the whole TARGET tree (not just modules) for IDBFS, syncfs, FS.mount, lidbfs, IndexedDB, OPFS and persistent-mount link flags (none), checked docs for a documented mount step (none), and that the Emscripten CI runs no storage test. The sibling runtime leaves mounting to application code.
reason: Nothing in CNA mounts a persistent file system, so under Emscripten's default in-memory FS every container and gamer-services write is lost on reload. The C ABI wasm target exports FS for the embedding page. Class fits its web-build peers; baseline Emscripten behaviour, unexecuted.
read: tree-wide search for IDBFS, syncfs, FS.mount, IndexedDB

refutation_attempt: Looked for a guard in both constructors and CreateWindow (none), then checked the claimed backend contrast: the X11 call sits in X11Platform::CreateWindow, not X11Window.cpp. Checked who can reach it: runtime code creates windows Windowed and later sets Exclusive or Windowed.
reason: Defect real against docs/platform-abstraction.md ('must refuse that mode'). Two details were off: X11 applies the creation mode in X11Platform::CreateWindow, not X11Window.cpp, and the XNA-facing runtime never requests BorderlessFullscreen, so only direct platform-layer callers reach it.

correction.expected: docs/platform-abstraction.md and IPlatformWindow::SetFullscreenMode state that “a window with no borderlessFullscreen capability must refuse that mode”, and the real backends enforce it uniformly: the Win32Window constructor and the CreateWindow functions of the X11, SDL2 and SDL3 platforms (modules/platform/src/X11/X11Platform.cpp, Sdl2Platform.cpp, Sdl3Platform.cpp) funnel a non-Windowed WindowDescription::fullscreenMode through SetFullscreenMode right after construction, so the refusal path runs. Headless and Terminal report borderlessFullscreen = false and their SetFullscreenMode throws PlatformNotSupportedException(BorderlessFullscreen).
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the Headless and Terminal window classes and CreateWindow functions, the Win32 window constructor, the X11, SDL2 and SDL3 CreateWindow functions and the conformance suite at 009d40f5. Not executed. The defect is that the two capability-minimal backends bypass their own refusal at construction; the real backends do not. The XNA-facing runtime cannot reach it: GraphicsDevice creates its window with the default Windowed mode and later calls SetFullscreenMode with ExclusiveFullscreen or Windowed only, so the path is reached only by code that calls IPlatform::CreateWindow directly with BorderlessFullscreen.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a deliberate SDL2 rationale or a compensating consumer (none; CNA's plan records the SDL3 pass-through as the established convention and Win32/X11/Wayland follow it). Checked SDL2 2.30.11: FLIPPED is set only in Cocoa and UIKit, values are already natural-adjusted, core does not negate.
reason: Sdl2Platform negates wheel x/y on SDL_MOUSEWHEEL_FLIPPED while Sdl3EventMapper passes them through, contradicting MouseWheelEvent's documented post-preference values and CNA's recorded convention. No test covers the SDL2 sign; the SDL3 mapper test pins pass-through. Low fits: SDL2 backend on natural-scrolling hosts.

refutation_attempt: Traced each early return and the ChangeDisplaySettingsExW result against the function's own comment ('a refusal is reported'), then SetFullscreenMode, which assigns fullscreenMode_ with no error path. Checked tests for an exclusive case (none). The monitor-query return repeats MonitorRect, so it is near-unreachable.
reason: The code contradicts its own comment: a failed display-mode change leaves a borderless window while GetFullscreenMode reports ExclusiveFullscreen and nothing is thrown. Realistic trigger is only a refused same-resolution change, so low fits. Win32 tests exercise SetFullscreenMode's borderless branch only.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether anything corrects 'granted' after creation (no query, granted = description), whether Win32Window feeds renderIntent or openGlFramebuffer (no), and how peers behave (SDL2/SDL3 query SDL_GL_GetAttribute). Verified no non-test caller of GetContextAttributes and both renderers request only depth 24, stencil 8, double buffer.
reason: Win32 returns the requested description as the granted one, contradicting IPlatformGlContext's 'attributes the context was actually created with', and DescribeFormat ignores channel and multisample fields. Real, but the in-tree blast radius is only the unreported legacy-context fallback. The Win32 test asserts only majorVersion > 0.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the unconditional capability and the capability-only Show* gate; peers derive the flag honestly. Looked for an observable Show* difference: the iOS dummy and an Emscripten Unix backend both call back synchronously with a null list, as FileDialog's own unavailable path does.
reason: Capability contradiction is real (a flag reporting true while SDL refuses, per the brief's lying-flag definition). But 'earlier timing' is wrong: both paths call back synchronously with an empty list, so only the capability value differs. SDL behaviour is read from source, not run on iOS or web.
read: local SDL 3 tree (newer than the pin): src/dialog/SDL_dialog.c, unix and dummy backends, CMakeLists.txt dialog selection

correction.actual: Sdl3Platform::GetCapabilities in modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3Platform.cpp sets capabilities.nativeFileDialog = true with no target condition, although primarySelection in the same function is guarded for Emscripten and Android and the X11 and Wayland platforms derive the flag from their dialog service. FileDialog::getIsSupportedProperty compensates with its own build-target switch (Web and iOS return false), but the three Show* functions, and any other reader of the capability, gate on the capability alone, so on those targets the request reaches Sdl3Dialogs and SDL. On iOS SDL builds its dummy dialog, which reports failure through the callback at once; in a browser SDL's Unix dialog code finds neither a desktop portal nor a helper process and does the same. ResultTrampoline in modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp turns SDL's null file list into an empty list, so the caller sees the same answer as a cancel, before Show* returns. That is also what FileDialog's own unavailable path delivers (ReportUnavailable calls back with an empty list immediately), so the result and timing a Show* caller observes are the same on both paths; what contradicts itself is the two public answers, the capability (true) and getIsSupportedProperty (false). The null parent window the candidate also lists is a documented note in modules/devices-ext/include/CNA/Devices/FileDialog.hpp and is not part of this defect.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the CNA sources at 009d40f5; not executed on iOS or in a browser. SDL's per-platform dialog selection was read in a sibling SDL checkout at exactly the revision TARGET pins (third_party/SDL at cbe3fbe9; re-read for the adversarial audit in CMakeLists.txt and include/build_config/SDL_build_config_ios.h): dialog sources are selected for Android, Unix, Haiku, Windows and macOS, and SDL_build_config_ios.h defines SDL_DIALOG_DUMMY, whose implementation calls the callback with a null list. For the web, a locally built Emscripten SDL 3 tree a few weeks newer than the pin shows that Emscripten's CMake platform file sets UNIX, so SDL compiles its Unix (portal and zenity) dialog sources there; at run time they find neither and call the callback with a null list at once, like the iOS dummy. FileDialog.hpp's statement that SDL has no dialog backend for Web is therefore imprecise as to the selection, but the conclusion that no dialog can be shown in a browser holds. The Emscripten reading was not made at the pinned revision.

refutation_attempt: Looked for deferral (worker thread, posted event) and for a CNA doc accepting synchronous Win32 dialogs: none. Show() is the modal COM call and onResult runs inline, cancel and creation-failure paths included. The X11 and Wayland portal tests assert the opposite.
reason: The three Win32Dialogs methods block in dialog->Show and call onResult before returning, contradicting IPlatformSystemServices ('after the Show* call has already returned', 'on the thread that pumps events') and FileDialog.hpp. Only the empty-callback refusal is tested. Low fits: modal blocking of a CNA-only extension.

refutation_attempt: Checked both trampolines and the devices-ext wrappers for any catch (none), and whether a CNA rule exists. Found docs/devices-event-contract.md section 6: exceptions must never cross a C callback boundary (log and continue), applied to sensors only. No test references either trampoline.
reason: Missing catch in ResultTrampoline and EntryClickTrampoline is real and reachable from FileDialog and SystemTray callbacks. The contract is stronger than the entry says: CNA's own devices event contract mandates catching at C callback boundaries, and the entry's 'or document it' alternative is looser than that policy.
read: tests tree search for Sdl3Tray, ResultTrampoline, EntryClickTrampoline

correction.expected: CNA's own devices event contract (docs/devices-event-contract.md, section 6, Exception semantics) states the decided policy: an unhandled exception escaping a user-supplied handler must never propagate across a C callback boundary, and the normative rule is log-and-continue, catching at the C-callback or thread-entry boundary and making the event observable. The Accelerometer and Gyroscope dispatch path follows it. FileDialog.hpp and SystemTray.hpp neither state that handlers must not throw nor catch on the caller's behalf.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. The contract is CNA's own devices event contract, section 6 of which is titled 'decided but not yet uniformly implemented' and lists sensor paths only, so the SDL3 dialog and tray boundaries are an unlisted instance of that policy. Neither devices-ext wrapper adds a catch (FileDialog.cpp passes the callback straight to the platform and SystemTray.cpp forwards it), so a handler's exception reaches the trampoline. What SDL's C frames then do with it (undefined behaviour, typically std::terminate) depends on the toolchain and was not run.
